headline: AMLC Chief Tells Impeachment Court Records Show ₱4.4 Billion in Duterte-Carpio Transactions
seoTitle: AMLC Chief Cites ₱4.4B in Duterte-Carpio Transactions
seoDescription: AMLC chief Ronel Buenaventura testified that covered and suspicious transaction reports involving VP Sara Duterte and Manases Carpio totaled about ₱4.4 billion.
deck: The total covers transaction reports from 2007 to 2025; Duterte's defense says the records do not prove illegal sourcing or wrongdoing.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Anti-Money Laundering Council Secretariat Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura told the Senate impeachment court that AMLC records contained about ₱4.4 billion in aggregate covered and suspicious transaction reports involving Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, from 2007 to 2025.

Buenaventura said the total included about ₱1.63 billion in inflows, ₱1.31 billion in outflows and roughly ₱1.46 billion that could not reliably be classified as either. He said the amount had been reduced from a previously cited ₱6.7 billion after a bank correction that AMLC validated.

sections.heading: What the records do not establish
paragraphs: A covered transaction report is triggered by statutory thresholds and is not by itself proof of a crime. A suspicious transaction report is a bank compliance report based on red flags; it is not a judicial finding of money laundering or unlawful income.

Duterte's defense argued that aggregated transaction totals can be much larger than the actual amount of distinct money involved and said the testimony did not prove that the funds came from illegal sources or the Chinese government. Those disputes remain for the impeachment court to assess.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The testimony is evidence presented by the House prosecution in an unresolved impeachment trial. It is not a conviction or a final factual finding. FMB News' earliest report on this trial is available at https://www.francinemariebautista.com/news/sara-duterte-impeachment-trial-defense-parallel-charges/.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The testimony places official financial-intelligence records before the impeachment court and may shape how senator-judges assess allegations about undeclared wealth and public trust. The legal significance of the records remains contested and unresolved.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The court is expected to examine bank and insurance records, the defense's explanations, and whether the reported flows are relevant to the constitutional charges. Any final conclusion rests with the senator-judges and is subject to applicable law and procedure.
